blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Along CP Garcia Avenue at the University of the Philippines (UP) Diliman, Quezon City, a 1.4-hectare property is reserved for a museum meant to keep alive the stories of Filipinos who suffered human rights violations under the regime of the late President Ferdinand Marcos Sr. Eight years after plans were formalized, however, no museum has risen on the site. Officially called The Freedom Memorial Museum, it remains in the preconstruction stage as the country marks the 54th anniversary of the declaration of martial law on Sept. 21, 1972.
